work_items: Implementation of Compact Parallax server-owned optimization control plane for concurrent development work
validations: Validation of optimized server-owned work using fast-lane validation for development acceleration

AC-01: validate protected requirement — Workstreams, contracts, validation gates and release gates form a canonical restart-safe DAG with stable identities, deterministic serialization/digesting, cycle detection and dangling-dependency rejection. Process recreation yields the same graph and scheduling inputs.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — Ready work is ranked by deterministic downstream blocking/remaining-cost signals with stable tie-breaking. Optimization targets validated outcome time and cannot grant mutation, lease, provider or deployment authority.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — Steal/reassignment proposals reference the existing worker execution and expected lease generation, require conflict-free path ownership and safe state, and are applied only through accepted P2-V0.16.1 CAS semantics. Stale generations or in-flight protected mutations/side effects fail closed.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — Server-owned integration capacity can defer lower-criticality work. Cancellation/supersession cannot interrupt an in-flight mutation, accepted-lineage transition or unrecorded side effect; absent a safe checkpoint the controller returns WAIT rather than forcing cancellation.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Impact selection is bound to a versioned graph digest and exact changed paths. Unknown/conflicting/low-confidence impact expands validation, mandatory global invariants are always included, and full protected suites remain mandatory at worker READY FOR INTEGRATION, integration and release boundaries.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — Reusable environments/caches are addressed by deterministic digest over approved secret-free toolchain/dependency/platform/config/source inputs. Missing or uncertain provenance invalidates reuse; secret-bearing material is rejected from identity and persisted metadata.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Pattern/component/config recommendations require immutable digest/version, validation provenance and compatibility predicates. Project/private scope is respected and use of a pattern never advances accepted lineage or satisfies validation without fresh evidence.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Failure/repair memory stores bounded structural fingerprints, repair class and outcome/provenance only. Raw private source/log/DOM/image/provider/prompt/credential/hidden-reasoning content is rejected, and Project-private memory cannot influence another Project.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Routing chooses only from approved model classes based on task capability/confidence and bounded cost/latency policy. It cannot alter Work Specification acceptance, evaluator thresholds, protected evidence precedence, tool/network/provider capabilities or production authority.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Preflight deterministically identifies cycles/missing dependencies, contradictory requirements, acceptance criteria without validation coverage, architecture/constitution conflicts, excess authority requests and ambiguous acceptance ownership. Material findings block implementation scheduling with typed evidence.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — Speculative candidates are immutable/disposable and explicitly cannot advance accepted lineage, merge/promotion gates or provider state. Sizing/rebalancing proposals preserve exactly one owner for every acceptance criterion and explicit dependency edges; orphaned/duplicate ownership is rejected.

AC-12: validate protected requirement — Phase telemetry covers queue/planning/generation/environment/build/test/browser/visual/provider/retry/integration/stall/human wait with bounded Project/run/workstream identity and evidence. It excludes private reasoning/raw content/secrets and supports lead-time, critical-path-blocked, retry/stall/human/integration-wait measures rather than treating occupancy/token throughput as the objective.
risks: Risk mitigation: Ensures correctness and protected authority dominance, with a focus on slower proven paths for uncertain impact and provenance
